title: Every bid recommendation on /draft ignores the user's remaining budget — with $4 left the board says "Win at $69 / Max bid $80 / Push up to $48"
claimUnderTest: draft-logic.js's header documents Winning bid(p) = min(Theoretical Max, topCompetitorMax + 1) and describes effectiveBudgetFor as 'the maximum $ a team can actually bid on a single player right now'. The /draft modal advertises an overpay guard.
observed: theoreticalMaxBid, myMaxBid, myWinningBid and enforceUpTo are computed from preDraft x aggression x tierInflation x phaseMultiplier and capped ONLY by topCompetitorMax + 1. Not one of them reads myRemaining or effectiveBudgetByIdx[myTeamIdx]. effectiveBudgetFor() is applied to RIVALS only (line 480-485 skips myTeamIdx). bidStatus() classifies against myWinningBid, so a bid 6x the user's cash reads 'Push up'. The only modal warning fires on amt > myWinningBid, never on amt > myRemaining, so entering an unaffordable amount below the ceiling shows nothing at all.

reproduction.expected: a bid ceiling <= myRemaining ($4), or an affordability warning
reproduction.actual: myRemaining=4, Sonny Styles myMaxBid=$80, myWinningBid=$69, enforceUpTo=$48, bidStatus($24) = {level:'push', label:'Push up'}

numericProof.formula: theoreticalMaxBid = floor(preDraft * (1 + aggression*(BA-1)) * inflation*tierMult * phaseMultiplier); myWinningBid = min(theoreticalMaxBid, topCompetitorMax + 1); NO min(..., myRemaining) term exists

userImpact: Mid-draft the user reads 'Win at $69' on a player they can only pay $4 for, bids, and either loses the auction after driving the price up or wins a bid they cannot fund. The bid-status chip actively says 'Push up' on an amount 6x their cash.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced at runtime with concrete numbers and the bidStatus consequence, which the prior finding did not quantify. The slot half of the prior finding is split out as W10-F002.

whatWorks: The rival-side ceiling (effectiveBudgetFor over other teams) is applied correctly and topCompetitorMax does cap the recommendation from above; the overpay banner fires correctly for the case it does cover (amount above the rival ceiling).
rootCause: myWinningBid was designed as 'the price that beats the field', and no second clamp for 'the price I can actually pay' was ever added. effectiveBudgetFor exists and would answer it, but is deliberately skipped for myTeamIdx.
requiredRepair: Clamp every emitted bid number by effectiveBudgetFor(myRemaining, mySlotsRemaining) and add an affordability state to bidStatus distinct from 'pass'. Add an amt > myRemaining branch to the modal warning.
dependencies: Depends on W10-F002 — mySlotsRemaining is currently wrong, so the clamp must not be built on the capped slot count.

title: mergeDraftCapitalTeams hard-caps every team's slot count at 6, so the user's team — which owns 31 of the 72 live picks — renders as "0/6 slots" with a 5.2x-wrong $/slot
claimUnderTest: The user's stated requirement is that the rookie auction optimizer has NO FIXED PLAYER SLOTS, no minimum and no maximum player count. draft-logic.js's own docstring says DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS 'only applies to a pristine workspace before the fetch completes' and that 'the actual per-team count is pulled from /api/draft-capital's picks array'.
observed: buildTeam() computes initialSlots = Math.min(feedSlots, DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS) — DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS = 6 is a hard MAXIMUM applied to the live feed, not a pre-fetch default. Live /api/draft-capital reports Russini Panini owning 31 picks and CollinFoz 7; both are clamped to 6. Total board slots collapse from 72 to 46. Everything downstream is wrong: slotPressure saturates at 1.0 after 6 picks (true 6/31 = 0.19), phaseMultiplier locks at its 1.5x maximum for the remaining 25 picks, effectiveBudget reserves $5 instead of $30, and mdv ($/slot) reads $114 instead of $22. Confirmed in the rendered DOM: the Teams panel prints '0/6' and 'MDV $114' for a $685 / 31-pick team, and the header phase card prints '6 of 6 slots'.

reproduction.expected: initialSlots 31 for Russini Panini, totalInitialSlots 72, mdv 685/31 = $22
reproduction.actual: initialSlots 6, totalInitialSlots 46, mdv $114, DOM shows '0/6' and '6 of 6 slots'

numericProof.formula: initialSlots = min(feedSlots, 6); mdv = remaining / slotsRemaining; slotPressure = 1 - slotsRemaining/initialSlots; phaseMultiplier = 1 + slotPressure*0.5

userImpact: The user's own team is modelled as having 6 roster spots when it has 31. After 6 picks the app declares the draft over for them — slots 0, effective budget $0, phase multiplier pinned at 1.5x, and the 'Spend up — don't let $ go unused' recommendation fires — while $679 and 25 picks are still live. Every MaxBid for the remaining 25 picks is inflated by 1.5/1.097 = 1.37x by the saturated phase multiplier.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced against the live feed and the rendered DOM, and quantified the four downstream consequences (slotPressure, phaseMultiplier, effectiveBudget, mdv) the prior finding named but did not measure.

whatWorks: slotsByTeamFromPicks() itself is correct — it returns the true 31/7/6/... counts from the live picks array. The corruption is introduced one function later.
rootCause: A single Math.min against a constant named 'DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS' that is being used as a maximum. In a league with pick trading the number of picks a team owns is unbounded above.
requiredRepair: Delete both Math.min(..., DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS) clamps in buildTeam(). Keep DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS strictly as the pre-fetch fallback its docstring describes.
dependencies: W10-F001's proposed budget clamp must land after this, or it will clamp against the wrong slot count.

title: There is no perfect-draft optimizer: the only recommender is an unconstrained per-player sort whose 'EV' is zero for every contested player, so the panel is EMPTY whenever budget advantage >= 1
claimUnderTest: Prompt section 26/27 asks whether the optimizer is a greedy value-per-dollar ranking or a real combinatorial optimizer. draft-logic.js documents nextBestTargets as an 'EV model' that ranks players 'by expected value'.
observed: Neither. grep for perfect.?draft / optimiz / knapsack / combinator over all .py/.js/.jsx finds nothing but a 'Nomination optimizer' comment. nextBestTargets scores each player independently as ev = max(0, inflatedFair - myWinningBid) * tagWeight + scarcityBoost, sorts, and slices to a fixed limit=5. It never enumerates subsets, never checks budget feasibility, and never considers a second player. It is not even greedy value-per-dollar: myWinningBid collapses to the CONSTANT topCompetitorMax+1 for every player whose ceiling clears the field, so the 'price' is identical ($19) for a $60 asset and a $1 asset — there is no per-dollar quantity to rank by. Worse, the surplus term is structurally zero whenever budgetAdvantage >= 1 and the top rival can still cover fair value (theoreticalMax >= inflatedFair, and the min() then returns inflatedFair), and the ev <= 0 filter drops those rows: measured 0 rows returned at BA 1.0, 1.1, 1.5 and 3.0, versus 3 rows at BA 0.33. The panel populates only when the user is POORER than the field or the field is bankrupt.

reproduction.expected: a budget-feasible recommended SET, or at minimum a non-empty ranked list at ordinary budget advantage
reproduction.actual: BA 1.0/1.1/1.5/3.0 -> 0 rows returned; at BA 3.25 the returned order is byte-identical to a plain preDraft-descending sort, and every row carries the same Win-at price of $19

numericProof.formula: ev = max(0, inflatedFair - myWinningBid) * tagWeight + scarcityBoost, where myWinningBid = min(theoreticalMax, topCompetitorMax+1) = 19 for all four rows

userImpact: There is no tool that answers 'given my $685 and my 31 picks, which set of rookies should I buy'. The one panel that looks like it answers that is blank for any user whose budget is at or above the league average — i.e. exactly the user this app was built for (live BA on /draft is 14.63x only because the slot cap of W10-F002 and the workbook budgets make it so). The requirement of no fixed player count is vacuously satisfied by there being no set-selection logic at all.

priorFinding.note: Prior said 'a preDraft sort wearing an EV model's clothes' — confirmed byte-for-byte on ordering. Extended with two facts the prior did not have: the price term is constant across players (so value-per-dollar is undefined), and the panel returns ZERO rows for BA >= 1.

whatWorks: The sort is stable and deterministic, the AVOID tag exclusion works, and the tier-scarcity boost is applied as documented.
rootCause: 'EV' was defined as surplus-against-my-own-winning-bid rather than value-per-dollar or a constrained subset objective. Because myWinningBid is derived from the same preDraft the surplus is measured against, the metric degenerates.
requiredRepair: Build the actual optimizer: a bounded knapsack over (expected clearing price, board value) with the budget as the capacity, NO slot cardinality constraint (per the stated requirement), allowing the empty set and unspent budget as valid answers. Keep nextBestTargets as a separate 'cheapest relative to fair' screen and rename its 'ev' field, which is not an expected value.
dependencies: Needs a per-player expected clearing price that is not a league-wide constant, and needs W10-F002 fixed so the budget capacity is real.

title: Vendor 'Market' dollars are normalized to $1200 over a different row count per vendor, so KTC overrates 44 of the 45 rookies it covers and underrates none
claimUnderTest: page.jsx documents the vendor dollars as making 'the vendorDollar - preDraft gap an honest "how many more dollars would a vendor-following leaguemate spend at this slot than my board does"'. nominationCandidates selects on vendorDollar > preDraft; bestValueOnBoard selects on preDraft > vendorDollar.
observed: Every vendor column is _rookie_dollars_from_values(values, total=1200) — the SAME $1200 pool spread over a DIFFERENT number of rows: 72 for our board, 45 for KTC, 63 for IDPTC. Mean dollar is therefore 1200/45 = $26.67 for KTC against 1200/72 = $16.67 for us, a pure artefact of coverage. On the live payload KTC's dollar exceeds ours for 44 of 45 covered rookies and is below ours for 0. Downstream: nominationCandidates ('vendor overrates us') fires on 51 of 72 rookies including the board's own #1; bestValueOnBoard ('we rate them above the market') finds ZERO qualifying offense rows and fills 8 of its 10 slots with backfill.

reproduction.expected: roughly balanced over/under counts between our board and a vendor board
reproduction.actual: KTC overrates 44, underrates 0; nominationCandidates returns 51/72; bestValueOnBoard offense qualifiers = 0

numericProof.formula: mean vendor dollar = 1200 / rows_covered; systematic lift = (1200/45) / 20.67 = 1.29x

userImpact: The 'Nomination targets' panel tells the user to nominate their own #1 rookie (Jeremiyah Love) on the grounds that KTC overrates him by $3.50 — the $3.50 is a normalization artefact, not a market read. The 'Best value on the board' panel can never surface a genuine offense bargain because the comparison is biased against it by construction.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced exactly on the live payload and quantified the 1.29x lift plus both downstream panel effects.

whatWorks: The Hill-curve dollar conversion itself is faithful — every column independently sums to exactly $1200, and the offense/IDP vendor routing picks the right vendor per row.
rootCause: Each vendor's ranking is converted to dollars against the full $1200 league pool regardless of how many rookies that vendor actually publishes, so coverage differences become value differences.
requiredRepair: Normalize each vendor over the pool value of the rows it covers (sum of OUR dollars for the same players), not over $1200. Or compare ranks rather than dollars.

title: 'Best value on the board' renders backfill rows as green underrate signals with a double-negative percentage — 8 of 10 live rows say the vendor UNDERRATES a player the vendor actually rates higher
claimUnderTest: bestValueOnBoard's docstring says the backfill exists so 'the panel always shows limit rows so the user can see what's still on the board even if we don't strictly outrate the market on every name' — i.e. backfill rows are explicitly NOT edge signals.
observed: The renderer does not distinguish qualified rows from backfill rows. It emits a hardcoded minus sign in front of the already-signed percentage — `−{Math.round(gapPct * 100)}%` — and a tooltip reading '{vendorLabel} underrates by {gapPct*100}%'. On the live board 8 of the 10 rows are backfill with NEGATIVE gapPct, so they render as e.g. '−-18%' with the tooltip 'KTC underrates by -18% (+$-11 board edge)' for Jadarian Price, whom KTC rates $11.50 ABOVE our board.

reproduction.command: node docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W10/probe-vendor-rowcount.mjs   # inspect the bestValueOnBoard rows and their gapPct signs
reproduction.expected: backfill rows rendered neutrally, or excluded from the edge styling
reproduction.actual: rows with gapPct -0.18, -0.16, -0.12, -0.06, -0.04, -0.03, -0.03, -0.01 rendered through the '−{pct}%' underrate template

numericProof.formula: gap = ourDollar - vendorDollar = -11.5; gapPct = gap/vendorDollar = -0.1797; rendered as '−' + round(gapPct*100) + '%'

userImpact: The panel headlined 'Best value on the board' presents the eight rookies the market most OVERRATES as the eight the market most underrates. A user shopping this panel buys exactly the players they should be selling.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced on the live board with the exact eight negative-gap rows.

whatWorks: The two qualified rows (CJ Allen +29%, Dillon Thieneman +7%) are correct and correctly signed.
rootCause: The backfill tier was added to guarantee a full panel, and the row template was reused verbatim without a qualified/backfill discriminator on the row objects.
requiredRepair: Stamp `qualified: true|false` on each row in bestValueOnBoard and render backfill rows with neutral styling and no percentage. Remove the hardcoded '−' and use the sign already carried by gapPct.
dependencies: Largely moot once W10-F004 is fixed — with an unbiased comparison the qualified tier will fill the panel — but the renderer bug should be fixed independently.

title: The inflation multiplier is unbounded and its degradation flag has no UI consumer — at pick 71 on the live pool a $1 rookie shows a fair price of $112 and a max bid of $168 with no warning
claimUnderTest: The in-file comment states: 'An absurd value substituted for an error is worse than no value, so degrade to "no global inflation" and say so; inflationDegraded lets the UI tell the user their PreDraft column is over-allocated instead of quietly showing four-figure fair prices.'
observed: Two problems. (1) grep for inflationDegraded across frontend/ returns draft-logic.js and __tests__ only — NO page or component reads it, so when the guard fires the UI silently switches to inflation=1 and says nothing. (2) The guard fires only once expectedPoolRemaining <= 0, i.e. strictly AFTER the divergence has already happened: inflation = remainingLeague / (totalBudget - soldPreDraft) has a pole as soldPreDraft approaches totalBudget, and the run below (live 72-rookie pool that sums to exactly $1200, every pick paid at 0.9x preDraft) reaches inflation 11.45x at pick 61 and 116x at pick 71 with inflationDegraded still false the whole way.

reproduction.expected: a bounded multiplier, or a degradation notice before four-figure-ratio prices appear
reproduction.actual: picks=61 inflation=11.45 degraded=false; picks=71 inflation=116.00 degraded=false, next undrafted preDraft=$1 -> FAIR=$112 MAX=$168

numericProof.formula: inflation = remainingLeague / (totalBudget - soldPreDraft) = 116 / 1 = 116; inflatedFair = floor(preDraft * inflation * tierMult)

userImpact: In the last dozen picks of a real draft the board tells the user a $1 rookie is worth $112 and that they may bid up to $168, with no warning banner. The arithmetic is not wholly fictional — money genuinely does chase a thin board late — but nothing caps it against the number of players left or against the user's cash (W10-F001), so the displayed number is unusable as guidance.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced with the real 72-row $1200 pool rather than the pristine board, which rules out the DEFAULT_ROOKIES $1211 mismatch (W10-F013) as the sole cause — the pole is in the formula itself.

whatWorks: The degradation branch itself is correct and does prevent the ~800x case the comment describes; soldPreDraft correctly uses the preDraftAtPick snapshot so retroactive edits do not rewrite history.
rootCause: An unbounded ratio with a guard placed at the far side of its own singularity, plus a status flag that was returned but never wired to a renderer.
requiredRepair: Cap the multiplier (e.g. remainingLeague / max(expectedPoolRemaining, undraftedCount)) and render inflationDegraded — and a new 'inflation clamped' state — as a visible banner on /draft.

title: /draft issues three /api/draft-capital fetches per load and two of them omit leagueKey, so the rookie pool and per-slot dollars always come from the default league
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Draft capital (per-team auction budgets, pick ownership)' follows leagueKey, and page.jsx line 3835 comments 'Scope the draft-capital fetch to the active league so per-team auction budgets come from the right Sleeper league.'
observed: Only fetchDraftCapital (line 3840) is scoped. The rookie-pool auto-sync (3597) and the 'Sync from contract' path (4210) both call the bare '/api/draft-capital' with no leagueKey, so they resolve to the user's activeLeagueKey pref or the registry default rather than the league selected on the page. With dynasty_new selected the page merges dynasty_new's 10-team budgets and slot counts against dynasty_main's 12-team / 6-round / 72-pick rookie pool and its per-slot dollar curve. Compounding this, the non-default league's payload carries no rookieName / rookieKtcValue at all (Sleeper-derived fallback), and rescaleValuesToBudget is called with a hardcoded 1200 regardless of league.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/draft-capital?leagueKey=dynasty_new' | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['numTeams'], d['draftRounds'], len(d['picks']), any(p.get('rookieName') for p in d['picks']))"
reproduction.expected: the /draft rookie pool and slot dollars to match the selected league's shape
reproduction.actual: dynasty_new returns numTeams=10 draftRounds=4 picks=80 rookieName-present=False, while the unscoped fetches return dynasty_main's 12/6/72 board with a full rookie pool

numericProof.formula: pool budget per league should be teamCount * per-team auction dollars; the page uses 1200 unconditionally

userImpact: A user on the second league sees the first league's rookie board and the first league's $1200/72-pick dollar curve stapled to their own team budgets. Nothing on the page says the two halves came from different leagues.

priorFinding.note: Prior flagged PickProjectorPanel mounting without a leagueKey. This is the same class of defect on two different call sites (the rookie-pool auto-sync and the contract sync), which the prior finding did not name.

whatWorks: fetchDraftCapital is correctly scoped and the backend honours leagueKey properly — the dynasty_new response is genuinely that league's rosters and traded picks.
rootCause: leagueKey scoping was retrofitted onto one of three fetch sites.
requiredRepair: Thread selectedLeagueKey through all three fetches and derive the rescale total from the league's registry roster settings instead of the constant 1200.

title: /api/draft-capital re-attempts a live keeptradecut.com scrape on every cache miss because only SUCCESS is memoized — the measured cold cost is 2.5s and the observed anonymous first hit was 13.2s
claimUnderTest: server.py's cache comment says the endpoint 'used to run ~4s of synchronous work — an openpyxl parse plus up to six blocking Sleeper calls' and that the 300s result cache plus threadpool offload solved it. _KTC_CACHE_TTL is documented as 6 hours.
observed: _get_ktc_rookies() writes _ktc_cache only when the live fetch SUCCEEDS. When KTC is unreachable or returns an unparseable page it returns None, falls through to the CSV, and caches nothing — so the next cache miss re-issues the same urllib.request.urlopen(timeout=15). Instrumented in-process against the live stack, _parse_draft_data logs 'KTC parse returned only 0 rookies, likely blocked' on every single invocation. Cost breakdown measured: openpyxl cold 1.27s / warm 0.64s, five Sleeper calls 1.20s total, _fetch_draft_capital end-to-end 2.5s per miss with everything warm and reachable. The route probe recorded 13.2s for the first anonymous request, and the backend log carries exactly one 'Sleeper API failed for draft capital team-name mapping: Connection reset by peer' at that timestamp. With six independent timeout=15 calls in the path the worst case is ~90s of a threadpool worker, and the 300s result TTL means the whole sequence repeats every 5 minutes for as long as the page is in use.

reproduction.command: ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1 .venv/bin/python -c "import time,server; [print(round((lambda t0: (server._fetch_draft_capital('dynasty_main'), time.time()-t0)[1])(time.time()),3)) for _ in range(2)]"
reproduction.expected: a memoized negative result and no repeated outbound KTC request per cache miss
reproduction.actual: 2.5s per call, 'KTC parse returned only 0 rookies, likely blocked' logged on every call

userImpact: Every 5 minutes one /draft or /league visitor pays the full cold cost — 2.5s when the network is healthy, 13.2s as actually measured here, and up to ~90s if any of the six upstreams hangs rather than resetting. On the public /league page that visitor is anonymous.

priorFinding.note: Not present in the area-0 prior finding set.

whatWorks: The result cache, the per-league asyncio single-flight and the run_in_threadpool offload all work correctly — the authenticated cache hit measured 6ms and 4ms, and the event loop is never blocked. The openpyxl workbook cache keyed on (path, mtime_ns, size) also works.
rootCause: _get_ktc_rookies memoizes the positive result only; there is no negative cache and no circuit breaker around a best-effort scrape that sits on the critical path of a user-facing endpoint.
requiredRepair: Memoize the failure with a short TTL (or a backoff), and move the KTC fetch off the request path entirely — it is a background-refresh concern, not a per-request one. Lower the per-call timeouts; 15s x 6 is far past any useful page budget.
dependencies: Pre-declared non-finding: the Sleeper connection reset itself is container egress. This finding is about the code's handling — unbounded retry with no negative caching — not the failure.

title: VERIFIED WORKING: the Sleeper-derived fallback's unpriced-pick exclusion behaves exactly as CLAUDE.md describes — 40 priced 2026 picks sum to exactly $1200 and 40 unpriced 2027 picks carry dollarValue null / isUnpriced true with no dilution
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: '_pick_value_from_contract returns None on a miss; build_sleeper_derived excludes unpriced picks from the dollar normalization (so they cannot dilute) and emits them with dollarValue: null + isUnpriced: true ... coveredPickYears is now derived from what was actually priced ... pricedPickCount / unpricedPickCount / unpricedPickYears make the omission visible.' The prior audit claimed the opposite — that 52% of the board is fabricated.
observed: Every element of the claim reproduces on the live non-default league. The response carries pricedPickCount 40, unpricedPickCount 40, coveredPickYears [2026], unpricedPickYears [2027]. The 40 priced picks sum to exactly 1200.0 with zero rounding drift; all 40 unpriced picks carry dollarValue null, adjustedDollarValue null and isUnpriced true while retaining real Sleeper ownership (currentOwner / originalOwner / isTraded). teamTotals sums to exactly 1200. No hardcoded 7000/4000/2000/1200-by-round value appears anywhere in the payload. The fabrication the prior audit reported is gone.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/draft-capital?leagueKey=dynasty_new' | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); ps=d['picks']; print(len(ps), sum(1 for p in ps if p.get('isUnpriced')), round(sum(p['dollarValue'] for p in ps if p['dollarValue'] is not None),4), sum(t['auctionDollars'] for t in d['teamTotals']), d['coveredPickYears'], d['unpricedPickYears'])"

numericProof.formula: sum(dollarValue for priced picks) == totalBudget AND all unpriced picks have dollarValue is None

userImpact: None — this is the correct behavior. Half the emitted board is honestly labelled unpriced rather than silently valued.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding's substance ('fabricates 52% of the board on live data') does NOT reproduce — the hardcoded round table is gone from the tree and the exclusion arithmetic is exact. The prior finding's secondary claim, that the 503 guard does not fire on a league mismatch, is TRUE but is a deliberate documented decision (Defect D-2 resolution in CLAUDE.md), not a defect.

whatWorks: Everything named in the claim, verified numerically.
requiredRepair: None. Note for the merge step: no frontend surface reads unpricedPickCount / unpricedPickYears / isUnpriced (only /trade reads coveredPickYears), so the backend's honesty is invisible to a /draft user — tracked separately, not blocking.

title: /api/draft-capital serves the hand-maintained per-pick dollar curve to anonymous callers on the stated grounds that it is 'already viewable on Sleeper', which is false for that column
claimUnderTest: The allowlist comment reads: 'Payload is public Sleeper data (team names, pick dollar values, owners) already viewable on Sleeper.'
observed: The redaction itself works — the anonymous response is 17,400 bytes against 25,472 authenticated, rookieName / rookiePos / rookieKtcValue / rookieKtcDollar / rookieIdpDollar are all stripped, and rookieBoardRedacted:true is stamped. But of the three field groups the comment calls 'already viewable on Sleeper', only two are: team names and pick ownership. dollarValue / adjustedDollarValue / originalDollarValue come from column L of CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx, a hand-maintained Hill-curve valuation the operator wrote — Sleeper publishes no such figure. teamTotals.auctionDollars is derived from the same column, so an anonymous caller reads every team's draft-capital valuation on the operator's own curve.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/draft-capital | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['rookieBoardRedacted'], d['picks'][0], d['teamTotals'][:2])"
reproduction.expected: either no proprietary valuation in the anonymous payload, or an allowlist comment that states accurately what is exposed
reproduction.actual: anonymous payload carries dollarValue 134.5 for pick 1.01 and auctionDollars 685 for the top team

numericProof.formula: anonymous payload retains dollarValue for all 72 picks, sourced from CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx L2:L73 which sums to 1200.0

userImpact: None to the user; this is an operator disclosure decision. It is reported because the justification recorded next to the allowlist entry is factually wrong for one of the three things it authorizes, so the decision was made on a false premise.

priorFinding.note: Not in the area-0 prior set.

whatWorks: _redact_draft_capital_for_public returns a copy and never mutates the shared cache, exactly as its docstring promises — verified by fetching anonymously then authenticated within the same 300s TTL window and confirming the authenticated response still carried all five private fields.
rootCause: The allowlist comment was written for the ownership data and not revised when the pick-value column was added to the payload.
requiredRepair: Operator decision. Either correct the comment to say the pick dollar curve is deliberately public, or add dollarValue/adjustedDollarValue/originalDollarValue/teamTotals to the redaction set and have the public /league tab render ownership only.
dependencies: tests/api/test_draft_capital_public_redaction.py pins the current field set and would need updating if the redaction widens.

title: hydrateWorkspace discards pos, assetClass, ktcDollar and idpTradeCalcDollar from every stored player on load, so the vendor panels are blank until a network refetch succeeds
claimUnderTest: hydrateWorkspace is the localStorage rehydration path for DRAFT_STORAGE_KEY; the vendor panels (nominationCandidates, bestValueOnBoard) select on p.ktcDollar / p.idpTradeCalcDollar / p.assetClass.
observed: Round-tripping a player through hydrateWorkspace reduces {id, rank, name, preDraft, pos, assetClass, ktcDollar, idpTradeCalcDollar} to {id, rank, name, preDraft}. Four of the eight fields — including both vendor dollars and the assetClass that the IDP/offense vendor routing was specifically written to depend on — are dropped. Both vendor panels therefore return zero rows on a cold load until the /api/draft-capital auto-sync lands, and stay empty for the whole session if that fetch fails (it is wrapped in a bare `if (!capitalRes.ok) return;`).
userImpact: On a page load where the draft-capital fetch is slow or fails — precisely a live-draft-night failure mode — the Nomination targets and Best value panels render empty with no explanation, and the IDP/offense vendor split silently falls back to the position string that assetClass exists to work around.
whatWorks: Picks, tags, target board, par sheet and nominations all survive hydration correctly; the auto-sync does restore the missing fields on a successful fetch.
rootCause: hydrateWorkspace rebuilds each player from an explicit whitelist that was not extended when pos/assetClass/vendor dollars were added to the player shape.
requiredRepair: Extend the player whitelist in hydrateWorkspace to carry pos, assetClass, ktcDollar and idpTradeCalcDollar.

title: Rookie pick values are point estimates everywhere on the live path — no mean/median/P10/P90/starter%/bust% distribution is served by any reachable route
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md describes a /draft 'Fundamental pick values (BDVM)' panel showing 'balanced-strategy pick EV / hit% / median / ceiling beside the market anchor, from buildBdvmPickRows', and config/bdvm/pick_outcomes_v1.json exists to supply pick outcome distributions.
observed: Every pick field the live board emits is a scalar: dollarValue, adjustedDollarValue, originalDollarValue, rookieKtcValue, rookieKtcDollar, rookieIdpDollar. There is no distributional field anywhere in the /api/draft-capital payload, and none in the frontend workspace shape. The only distribution machinery in the repo is BDVM's, and GET /api/bdvm/values returns status 'no_projection_snapshot' because data/bdvm/ does not exist in this container — so the /draft BDVM pick panel and the 'Fund gap' column self-suppress and the user sees point estimates only. Separately, the only blanket multiplier over picks is config/weights/pick_year_discount.json's offsetDiscounts {0:1.00, 1:0.82, 2:0.66, 3:0.53}, which is applied per YEAR to every pick of that year regardless of round or slot — that lives on the /api/data board, not on the draft board, which applies no multiplier at all.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/bdvm/values | head -c 200; echo; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/draft-capital | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(sorted(json.load(sys.stdin)['picks'][0].keys()))"
reproduction.expected: distributional fields (p10/p50/p90/hitRate) on pick rows, or an ok BDVM payload supplying them
reproduction.actual: BDVM: {"status":"no_projection_snapshot"}; draft-capital pick keys are all scalars: adjustedDollarValue, dollarValue, isExpansion, isTraded, originalDollarValue, originalOwner, overallPick, pick, pickInRound, currentOwner, round, rookieIdpDollar, rookieKtcDollar, rookieKtcValue, rookieName, rookiePos

numericProof.formula: count of fields matching /p10|p50|p90|median|hitRate|bust|ceiling/ across the live pick payload

userImpact: The user cannot see the variance on a pick. A 1.01 and a 1.12 are both single numbers with no indication that the 1.01's outcome distribution is far tighter, which is the single most decision-relevant fact when trading picks for players.

priorFinding.note: Not in the area-0 prior set; the prior audit did not test the distribution question.

whatWorks: config/bdvm/pick_outcomes_v1.json and the BDVM pick-EV code path exist and are wired; the endpoint degrades honestly rather than fabricating.
rootCause: data/bdvm/projections/ is absent (pre-declared audit-harness condition). Independently of that, the draft board itself was never designed to carry distributions.
requiredRepair: Populate data/bdvm/projections/ to activate the existing pick-EV panel, and separately decide whether the /draft market board should carry a distribution of its own.
dependencies: Blocked on the absent path data/bdvm/projections/ — pre-declared non-finding for the 503 itself; reported here only to answer the distribution question factually.

title: Displaced-player cost is not charged at all: computeRosterBreakdown's shortages feed nothing, and DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS is invented rather than read from the league's roster settings
claimUnderTest: Prompt section 26/27 asks whether displaced-player cost is charged once or double counted. The /draft page renders a roster-gap strip from computeRosterBreakdown.
observed: Neither once nor twice — it does not exist. grep for /displac/i over all .py/.js/.jsx in the repo returns only rank-displacement code in src/league_intel/ and a TE-premium comment; there is no roster-displacement or opportunity-cost term anywhere in the draft path. computeRosterBreakdown produces counts / needPositions / shortages, and page.jsx consumes them for exactly one thing: a decorative chip strip at line 4802. No bid function, no EV term, no recommendation and no sort key reads needPositions or shortages. Separately DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS = {QB:3, RB:4, WR:5, TE:2, DL:3, LB:3, DB:3} is a hardcoded guess; the registry publishes this league's real starters block (QB 1, RB 2, WR 3, TE 2, FLEX 2, SFLEX 1, K 1, DL 3, LB 3, DB 3) and rosterSize 58, and nothing reads it.

reproduction.command: grep -rn -i 'displac' --include=*.js --include=*.jsx --include=*.py . | grep -v node_modules | grep -v .venv; grep -n 'needPositions\|shortages' frontend/app/draft/page.jsx
reproduction.expected: a cost term subtracted from a bid or EV when a new player displaces an existing starter
reproduction.actual: zero displacement code in the draft path; needPositions/shortages appear only in the line 4802 chip strip

numericProof.formula: count of code paths where shortages/needPositions alter a bid, EV, or ordering

userImpact: The board will happily recommend a fourth tight end at full price with no discount for the fact that the user cannot start him, and will not surface a discount on a position where they have a genuine starter hole. The roster-gap chips imply positional need is being accounted for; nothing accounts for it.

priorFinding.note: Confirms both PRIOR-A00-F09 (nothing reads the roster-needs strip) and PRIOR-A00-F10 (DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS is invented and ignores the league's roster settings); merged here because they are one gap.

whatWorks: computeRosterBreakdown's counting and shortage arithmetic are correct in isolation, and the chip strip renders accurately.
rootCause: The roster-need input was built and surfaced but never connected to the valuation.
requiredRepair: Read positionMins from the resolved league's rosterSettings.starters, and add a displacement/marginal-starter term to the bid model — charged exactly once, at the point the board value is converted to a bid.
dependencies: Should be built together with the real optimizer (W10-F003) so the displacement term enters the objective rather than being bolted onto a per-player score.

title: src/api/auction_power.py declares itself the source of truth for effective auction power but has zero production callers — only tests import it
claimUnderTest: The module docstring: 'This module remains the source of truth + the home of the Phase 2 simulation and the unit tests.'
observed: grep for effective_auction_power over all non-venv .py returns the definition, tests/api/test_auction_power.py and tests/api/test_auction_power_parity.py — and nothing else. server.py never imports it and no route serves it. The live lens is frontend/lib/auction-power.js, consumed by frontend/app/league/sections/draft-capital.jsx, _trade-simulator.jsx and lib/trade-logic.js. The docstring itself concedes this two lines earlier ('the live UI lens is currently computed client-side ... keep them in lockstep') while still asserting the Python module is authoritative.

numericProof.formula: count of non-test Python modules importing effective_auction_power

userImpact: None directly. The risk is drift: two implementations of a numeric lens where only one is live and the dead one is labelled authoritative. tests/api/test_auction_power_parity.py exists to bind them and passes today (10 passed, python 3.11.15).

priorFinding.note: Reproduced; additionally ran the parity test, which passes, so the two implementations do agree today.

whatWorks: The parity test genuinely binds the two and currently passes.
rootCause: Phase 1 was implemented in Python for testability, then reimplemented in JS for the client, and the Python docstring was never demoted.
requiredRepair: Either serve the lens from Python via a route, or relabel the Python module as the reference implementation and name the JS file as the live path.

title: DEFAULT_ROOKIES sums to $1211 against a comment claiming $1200, pulling the inflation singularity 11 dollars inside the draft on a pre-sync board
claimUnderTest: The comment above DEFAULT_ROOKIES: 'Verbatim from the Inflation tab (columns A-C). Sums to $1200 to keep the league-wide accounting consistent with the sheet.'
observed: The 72 preDraft values sum to 1211, not 1200. DEFAULT_TEAMS' budgets do sum to exactly 1200. Because inflation = remainingLeague / (totalBudget - soldPreDraft), the denominator crosses zero after 61 of 72 picks instead of at the last pick, and on a simulated draft paying 0.9x preDraft the multiplier reaches 111x at pick 60 while inflationDegraded is still false. On the live board this is moot — the auto-synced pool from /api/draft-capital sums to exactly 1200.0 (verified on all 72 rookieKtcValue entries) — so the impact is confined to a pristine or offline workspace.
userImpact: A user who opens /draft with the network down, or before the first sync lands, gets a board whose late-draft prices blow up 11 picks early. With the network up the live pool overwrites it.

priorFinding.note: The arithmetic is confirmed exactly. The prior's causal claim — that this mismatch 'is what breaks late-draft inflation' — is REFUTED: W10-F006 reproduces the same divergence on the live $1200 pool, so the pole is in the formula and the $11 only moves it earlier.

whatWorks: The live auto-synced pool sums to exactly 1200.0, so the seed mismatch is latent in normal operation.
rootCause: Hand-transcribed seed data drifted from its source sheet.
requiredRepair: Rescale the seed pool to 1200, and add an assertion so the two constants cannot drift again.
dependencies: Does not fix W10-F006, which is independent.

title: NOT REPRODUCIBLE: draft-capital team totals accumulate workbook column Q while the emitted per-pick dollars come from column L, but the two columns are byte-identical today so no defect is observable
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A00-F17 asserts the per-team dollar totals are summed from a different workbook column than the per-pick dollars the UI displays, so the two can disagree.
observed: The code divergence is real: the emitted dollarValue / adjustedDollarValue / originalDollarValue all come from pick_values_per_slot (column L2:L73), while team_totals_decimal[owner_team] += float(val) accumulates the Q-column value. But reading the live workbook, Q45:Q116 and L2:L73 are identical in all 72 rows (max abs difference 0.0) and both sum to 1200.0. Summing the live payload's adjustedDollarValue per currentOwner reproduces teamTotals exactly (684.5->685, 180->180, 119->119, 110.5->111, 74->74, ...) within largest-remainder rounding. No observable defect exists today.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import openpyxl; wb=openpyxl.load_workbook('CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx', data_only=True); ws=wb['Draft Data']; Q=[ws.cell(r,17).value for r in range(45,117)]; L=[ws.cell(r,12).value for r in range(2,74)]; print(sum(Q), sum(L), sum(1 for q,l in zip(Q,L) if abs(q-l)>1e-9))"
reproduction.expected: a measurable divergence between the two columns if the prior finding is live

userImpact: None today. The latent risk is that the workbook is hand-maintained, so the operator can desynchronize Q from L at any time and the totals would then silently disagree with the displayed per-pick values.

priorFinding.note: The code path the prior finding describes is exactly as described, but the current workbook data makes it a no-op. Recording as a verified negative rather than inheriting the claim.

whatWorks: teamTotals sums to exactly 1200 via _round_to_budget largest-remainder rounding, and per-owner sums of the displayed L values match the emitted totals.
rootCause: Two reads of what is meant to be the same quantity.
requiredRepair: One-line change: accumulate `dollar` rather than `val` into team_totals_decimal, so the totals are provably the sum of what is displayed.

title: The /draft overpay warning renders a doubled dollar sign on the rival-ceiling figure ('$$175')
claimUnderTest: The overpay banner is meant to read 'The top rival can only bid $175'.
observed: The JSX is `The top rival can only bid $\n{fmt$(stats.topCompetitorMax)}`. The literal `$` is JSX text and fmt$() already prepends its own `$` (line 131: return `${sign}$${...}`), so the rendered string is '$$175'. The other three figures in the same banner use the `${amt}` form where the `$` is text and `{amt}` is the raw number, which is correct.

reproduction.actual: a literal '$' immediately followed by fmt$()'s own '$'

numericProof.formula: rendered prefix = literal '$' + fmt$ output which itself starts with '$'

userImpact: Cosmetic only — the banner is legible, just wrong. Included because it sits inside the one guard rail the bid engine has (see W10-F001) and signals that the banner is untested.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed by static reading of both the template and fmt$. Not confirmed in the rendered DOM — the banner requires opening the record-pick modal with an over-ceiling amount, which was not exercised in the page probe; hence confidence medium rather than high.

whatWorks: The banner's trigger condition (amount above myWinningBid on my own team) is correct for the case it covers.
rootCause: Mixed use of the `${literal}{expr}` and `{fmt$(expr)}` idioms in one string.
